proposal.name: Ratify and run native acceptance tests

issue_plan.name: Ratify and run native acceptance tests
issue_plan.summary: Pin native acceptance sources, repository parts, frameworks, exact selectors and captured execution configuration while preserving existing Go hashes and locks. Four ordered issues add the shared ratification contract, independent Go execution, pytest, then Vitest and Jest with mixed-framework coverage. Each test must independently fail on base and pass on the candidate with completed framework evidence. Every step updates SPEC.md, README.md and docs/factory.md, and its merger records the decision before the next step.

issues.title: Pin native acceptance identities without changing existing Go locks
issues.body:
Issue #501, step 4 of #452's ratified plan, requires plumbing acceptance tests in the configured repository's own framework. internal/plumbing/plan.go currently admits only Go functions; the configured sandbox has no individual acceptance evidence. Establish the shared identity and its consumers; unsupported execution refuses plans until the following adapters merge.

Extend the plan's test representation with an explicit repository part, framework and exact selector, together with its repository-relative source file and human-readable assertion. Recognize Go testing, pytest, Vitest and Jest as distinct frameworks, compatible with the captured part's language. Native identity is the full tuple of part, framework, file and selector, not the display name. Selectors identify a single Go test in its package and declared file, a complete pytest node ID, or a Vitest/Jest test's complete nested title within an exact file. Parameterized cases need an exact case identity; a group or pattern selecting multiple cases is not one acceptance test. Validate clean paths, source-file conventions, nonempty selectors, part ownership and directory containment, language/framework agreement, and executable test_one availability. Reject duplicate full identities, inconsistent file/selector combinations and incomplete native metadata. Legitimate spaces and punctuation in native names are data, never shell syntax. Go-only declaration and Test-name checks remain specific to Go; do not pretend a Go AST can validate Python or TypeScript declarations. Runtime discovery in later steps must establish native declarations and uniqueness.

Read acceptance sources verbatim from new regular files under tests/ at their repository paths; reject links, unsafe ancestors, existing base files, extra source entries and overlap with writable production files. Hash and store all execution identity and exact source bytes. Obtain execution authority from the trusted caller's captured repository snapshot, never an agent-supplied digest or candidate contract. Bind a deterministic content identity of the captured repository contract, including part directory, language, image and test_one command, and the captured declared inputs relevant to selection; retain base revision provenance without requiring an unrelated commit with identical execution configuration to invalidate the plan. Missing authority or a different execution identity must refuse execution before dependency preparation. Candidate configuration edits cannot replace the captured policy, and a later snapshot cannot silently reinterpret a ratified selector.

Preserve the legacy Go representation, canonical hash bytes and lock validity exactly when native metadata is absent. Existing Invariant plans need no migration, rewrite or repository.json. Never infer a new framework or default part into an old hashed plan. Reject malformed or partial native records rather than downgrading them to legacy. New metadata changes must invalidate the ratified hash just as source edits do, and ordering of equivalent file/test declarations must remain deterministic.

Update draft reading and final proposal creation, hashing, lock writing/reading, saved proposal and revision round trips, ratification verification, source staging and scope consumers together. Proposal displays must expose the full identity being ratified and render source with the correct language, with names safely displayed as text. Configured planning/check callers must carry the same trusted snapshot; the separate build test tool continues to use the queue's registered authority, not policy supplied over IPC. Builders and repairs cannot alter the new tests or their selectors; staging and scope retain the fixed original baseline and existing regression-file allowance. Keep external intake and regression scope unchanged.

Add identity fields to configured acceptance results and diagnostics now, retaining legacy Go result behavior. Configured results with no supported adapter or no completed individual evidence must explicitly be unstarted/refused and cannot fall through Check's legacy Accepted-only logic. A suite exit status never supplies an individual pass or base failure. Until the following issues implement execution, native drafts can be read and round-tripped but cannot be proposed on absent evidence.

Acceptance must cover all four identity forms; independent same-named tests in different files or parts; duplicate and ambiguous identity refusals; exact source preservation; lock and saved-proposal round trips; source, selector, part, framework and authority tampering; changed versus unchanged captured execution configuration; unsafe paths and links; and protection through staging and scope. Pin expected hashes from pre-change Go plans and exercise existing committed Invariant locks without rewriting them. Show that unsupported native execution, setup failure and suite-only success cannot qualify a draft or build. Use ordinary Go tests and temporary repositories without Docker/network.

Update SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md to describe the new ratification contract and the still-pending adapters, placing schema and selector detail in docs/factory.md. Keep external plumbing explicitly disabled and the existing Invariant Go path operational. Foundations are D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0121, D-0122, D-0162, D-0173, D-0281, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305, plus #452's ratified plan and #484's captured execution API. The merger records the extension of D-0107 before the next issue; the build cannot write decisions/. Changed SPEC bullets cite their foundations without inventing decision IDs. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work; affected CI Python/TLAPS suites remain required.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Run configured Go acceptance tests with independent completion evidence
issues.body:
Continue #501, step 4 of #452's ratified plan, after the native identity contract has merged. Plans now pin source, part, framework, file, selector and captured configuration, but configured suite commands alone establish no acceptance outcome. Implement the common offline acceptance lifecycle and the Go adapter through each part's declared test_one command. Keep Invariant's existing unconfigured Go runner, hashes and locks compatible.

Use the captured RepositoryChecks snapshot and verified dependency environment already provided by internal/plumbing/repository_checks.go, repository_docker.go and dependencies.go. Execute every acceptance selector separately in its owning part, with the pinned source bytes and execution identity. Apply safe framework-specific argument construction to test_one's single {test} placeholder, including exact name matching and package/file qualification. Preserve the declared command's execution policy; refuse templates that cannot safely select the required test rather than guessing or running a different command. A template that interpolates the selector into shell or interpreter source is not supported. Selector data must not become options, glob expansion, shell evaluation or an unescaped regular expression. Framework adapters may constrain selection and attach trusted evidence collection, but may not enable networking, installation or downloads during checks.

Extend the trusted host/container interface to collect framework completion evidence separately from stdout/stderr diagnostics. Bind each invocation and result to its part, framework, file and selector, and accept only one unambiguous matching completed selection. Go must confirm that the declared function belongs to the ratified file and selected package, including distinguishing same-named tests in other packages or parts. Collect Go testing lifecycle and terminal evidence rather than inferring completion from exit status, a textual PASS/FAIL line, or a fabricated JSON/runner marker. Reject absent or duplicate selections, skipped tests, zero-test success, truncated or conflicting evidence, stale records from a previous invocation, and records for another file or part. A nonzero process exit without attributable framework evidence is not automatically a test failure.

Make Check demand completed failure evidence separately for every acceptance test before a proposal can be produced, and make candidate Passed require all configured phases and all acceptance tests to pass. An already-passing selector invalidates the draft even if another selector fails. Expected base test/compile failures must not prevent the independent checks needed to establish each selector's result; provide a base-check path that does not simply stop at the existing first failing suite command. A format, lint, install, tool-launch or unrelated setup failure supplies no acceptance evidence. The candidate still fails its ordinary command checks, and missing individual evidence never becomes success. Preserve completed Go compiler failures attributable to the proposed API as eligible base evidence, including separate attribution to the selected acceptance package; missing tools, unresolved dependencies, broken discovery, unrelated package failures and interrupted compilation do not qualify. Distinguish completed assertion/panic failures from incomplete runs.

Use one shared whole-run deadline and test-phase allowance across suite and acceptance invocations, across all parts, with no renewal. Preserve offline pinned images, resource limits, at most one active candidate environment, cleanup with its bounded uncanceled context and queue ownership through cleanup. Install failures, timeouts, cancellation, startup failure and cleanup failure cannot make a draft qualify, even after a completed test failure. Retain completed and unfinished identities and failure reasons in structured results and summaries, without allowing clipped output to erase them. The separate builder test tool and fresh final checks must use identical source, identity, evidence rules and registered authority. Leave pytest, Vitest and Jest explicitly unsupported until their adapters merge.

Acceptance must exercise a small real Go fixture that fails on base and passes after a production change with unchanged tests; two acceptance tests in one package where only one initially fails; identical names in different packages/parts; wrong-file and multiple-match refusals; a new-API compile failure that becomes a real candidate pass; and setup/compiler failures that must not qualify. Cover skipped and absent tests, zero-test success, exit without running tests, duplicate/stale evidence, fabricated stdout and stderr lifecycle records, panic completion, deadlines and cancellation after an earlier failure. Include source/configuration/selector mismatch before execution and an IPC builder fixture showing tool and final checks agree. Default Go tests exercise orchestration and evidence without Docker/network, including real Go testing; add an opt-in pinned-image fixture for preparation, execution and cleanup. Preserve Invariant's existing acceptance suite.

Update SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md in this change to describe configured Go acceptance execution, completion criteria, safe test_one forms, the failure-versus-setup distinction and remaining framework support. External repository intake remains disabled. Foundations are D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305, #452's ratified plan, #484's execution API and the preceding identity change. The merger records the execution decision before the next issue; the build cannot write decisions/. Changed SPEC bullets cite their foundations. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work; affected CI Python/TLAPS suites remain required.

issues.title: Collect exact pytest acceptance results in the offline runner
issues.body:
Continue #501, step 4 of #452's ratified plan, after native ratified identities and configured Go acceptance execution have merged. Implement the pytest adapter using the same captured configuration, independent invocation, result identity and offline dependency environment. Python acceptance files are new regular framework-discoverable test files whose exact bytes are pinned by the plan; they no longer need Go syntax or Test-prefixed names.

Run the declared Python part's test_one command once per exact file-qualified pytest node ID, relative to that part. Support functions, class methods and an explicitly selected parameterized case. Match literal paths and IDs, including punctuation and spaces in parameter IDs, without shell evaluation or broad -k expression matching. Require exactly one matching collected test; a class, file, ambiguous selector or parameter group selecting several cases is not one acceptance test. Use the preceding step's validation of part, framework, source and captured execution authority and refuse unsafe command templates before launching anything. Pytest and its dependencies must already be present in the locked prepared environment; the check never fetches them.

Collect lifecycle evidence through a factory-controlled pytest integration, not parsed console summaries. Bind collection, execution and terminal status to the invocation and exact node ID, and isolate evidence from captured test output. Require completion of the selected call and the run, including teardown, for a candidate pass. Tests with the same function or method name in another file or part cannot satisfy the selector. Skips, expected failures, unexpected-pass/xfail bookkeeping, collection deselection, no-tests success, duplicate IDs, absent calls, incomplete runs and conflicting evidence do not count as a normal pass or an attributable base assertion failure. Missing pytest, plugin/import configuration errors, fixture setup/teardown failures and dependency/environment failures must be classified as setup failures, not evidence that the proposed behavior is absent.

Retain the common exception for attributable code failures without weakening setup refusal. A completed collection/import failure can qualify only when evidence establishes that it comes from the selected acceptance source's use of a missing proposed application API, or the application code it targets, with a working admitted framework and dependencies; unrelated imports, a missing third-party distribution, broken conftest, malformed test setup or ambiguous attribution must refuse the draft. Test the positive proposed-API case and nearby setup-failure cases. A terminal nonzero status or diagnostic text alone never establishes this attribution. Completed assertion failures qualify on the base, and every same selector must later have a normal completed pass on the candidate.

Retain shared phase/whole-run deadlines, cancellation, queue, cleanup, source protection and captured dependencies. Timeout or interruption invalidates base evidence even after an earlier failure. Reports retain full identities; draft, builder-tool and final checks use the same adapter without suite-only or legacy fallback.

Acceptance must demonstrate independent fail-on-base/pass-after-change pytest fixtures with unchanged acceptance source and selector, including two same-named files, two Python parts, class methods and a selected parameterized case with punctuation. Cover one already-passing test alongside a failing one; absent, skipped, xfail, duplicate and multi-match selections; zero-test success; setup/teardown and missing-tool failures; attributable versus unrelated import failures; incomplete execution, deadlines and cancellation; forged stdout/stderr reporter text and replayed evidence; and source/selector/configuration tampering. Exercise the real pytest integration in a pinned offline fixture using existing dependency preparation, not merely a fake that returns desired result records. Keep default Go orchestration and evidence regression tests runnable without Docker/network and provide an opt-in real pinned-image suite that fails rather than skips when enabled and its prerequisites are unavailable. Existing Go tests and lock compatibility must remain intact.

Update SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md with pytest support, exact selector examples, evidence and setup-failure rules, supported pinned fixture versions and the remaining TypeScript work. External plumbing remains disabled. This rests on D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305, #452's ratified plan and the preceding identity/execution changes. Changed SPEC bullets cite their foundations. The merger records the pytest decision before the next issue. Recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work; affected CI Python/TLAPS suites remain required.

issues.title: Collect exact Vitest and Jest acceptance results and complete native coverage
issues.body:
Complete #501, step 4 of #452's ratified plan, after the common native identity, configured Go runner and pytest adapter have merged. Add separate Vitest and Jest adapters for TypeScript parts using the same ratified source, part/framework/file/selector identity, captured test_one command, verified dependency environment and completion criteria. Include the cross-framework fixtures and documentation that complete #501.

Accept new regular TypeScript test files following Vitest/Jest test/spec conventions, including TSX where the configured framework supports it. Select one exact file and its complete nested test title through the declared test_one command. Escape title punctuation as literal matching data and constrain file selection so a same-named test in another file, part or framework cannot satisfy it. Names containing spaces, quotes, regular-expression metacharacters or shell punctuation must stay inert arguments. Use one-shot execution, never watch mode. Refuse unsafe or unsupported templates rather than interpreting selector text as source or silently substituting another command. Test.each/it.each cases qualify only when the resulting full title selects exactly one concrete case; duplicate titles or a pattern selecting several cases are ambiguous and must fail.

Use factory-controlled framework reporters/integrations for collection and terminal execution evidence, with Vitest and Jest interpreted according to their own lifecycles. Bind records to the exact invocation, framework, part, file and title. Application console output and fabricated JSON, TAP, JUnit, PASS/FAIL text or existing runner markers must remain diagnostics. Missing, stale, conflicting, duplicate, truncated or mismatched result artifacts cannot count as evidence, even if the command exits zero. Guard the evidence transport against candidate-provided replacement reporters or prewritten artifacts. A normal terminal test pass and completed successful invocation are required on the candidate; no-tests success, skipped/todo tests, expected-failure bookkeeping, a selected test that never runs, worker death and incomplete shutdown are not passes.

Run each selector independently and reject a proposal if any already passes, is absent, is skipped or lacks completed attributable failure evidence. Keep assertion failures distinct from hooks/setup, transforms, configuration loading, missing runners, missing npm dependencies and install/tool errors. Preserve analogous proposed-API failure evidence only when a completed transform/import/type failure is demonstrably attributable to the selected test's use of proposed application code with a working configured framework and admitted dependencies; ambiguous failures and malformed acceptance setup refuse the draft. Cover a positive proposed-API case for each framework alongside missing-dependency and broken-configuration counterexamples. Candidate acceptance still requires the actual selected test to complete and pass.

Share the existing whole-run and test-phase budgets across parts and selectors, with no renewal, retaining offline execution, resource limits, one active candidate environment and bounded cleanup. Vitest/Jest and their transforms come from captured locked dependencies; do not install or download during the check or introduce a Python requirement in Node images. Preserve full per-test identity and failure reasons in tool results, final checks and summaries, and keep source/selector/configuration mismatch refusal in front of execution. Preserve these identities throughout ratification.

Acceptance must use distinct real Vitest and Jest fixtures that independently fail on the base and pass after a production change without changing their ratified tests. Cover nested titles, punctuation, one exact parameterized case, duplicate titles, same names in different files and different parts, one passing selector beside a failing selector, skips/todo/expected failures, absent selection, no-tests success, setup and tool failures, attributable code failures, incomplete workers, deadlines and cancellation, and forged or replayed diagnostics/artifacts. Provide default offline Go tests for orchestration, argument safety, evidence validation and reporting, plus opt-in pinned-image fixtures for both actual frameworks with locked npm inputs, failing on unavailable prerequisites when enabled. Fakes alone cannot establish framework integration.

Finish with a mixed configured repository fixture containing Go, pytest, Vitest and Jest parts, with deliberately colliding display names wherever the frameworks permit them. Check each selector separately on base and candidate; changing one part must not satisfy another's failing selector. Demonstrate that source, selector, part, framework and captured configuration tampering invalidates ratification/execution, including through the separate builder tool and fresh final-check path. Re-run fixed legacy Go hash/lock fixtures and the existing Invariant acceptance behavior to demonstrate migration-free compatibility. Include stale evidence from a previous base/candidate invocation and a suite that prints forged success while the selected test is absent. Exercise both per-adapter evidence and aggregate Check/Passed decisions.

Update SPEC.md, README.md (at most 400 lines) and docs/factory.md to describe all four working native acceptance frameworks, selector and file conventions, supported fixture versions, safe test_one examples, configuration binding and completed failure/pass requirements. Remove the statement that native acceptance evidence is later work; keep external repository intake disabled because #452 enables that separately. This rests on D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301 and D-0305, #452's ratified plan and the preceding native acceptance changes. Changed SPEC bullets cite their foundations. The merger records the TypeScript/native acceptance decision before #452's next step; the build cannot write decisions/. Recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work; affected CI Python/TLAPS suites remain required.
